Eva pulled her coat tighter around her, the fabric rough against her skin, a reminder of the chill that settled in her bones. He stepped closer, his eyes darting back toward the mouth of the alley where the streetlights were few and far between. “I think someone’s following us.”

Eva’s heart quickened, pounding a staccato beat against her ribs. She glanced over her shoulder, half-expecting to see a figure lurking in the shadows. Just the wind, she told herself, but a thread of unease coiled tight in her stomach. “Are you sure?” she asked, her voice barely above a whisper. “It could just be the wind.”

“Yeah, right,” Marco scoffed, but his bravado faltered as he scanned the darkened street. “Let’s just hurry up. I don’t want to stick around to find out.”
